implementation_notes: SwiftNIO is the ecosystem's networking core, and it solves the same problem with a different arrangement: MultiThreadedEventLoopGroup creates a number of threads with pthreads and places one SelectableEventLoop - a kqueue/epoll selector - on each, and a listening socket is registered on one loop whose accepted channels are then spread across the group. Each loop has one permanent leader (its thread), no handle set is shared between threads and there is no promotion protocol, while the pattern's goals - kernel-side readiness, bounded threads, no thread-per-connection - are met. Hand-write the classic shared-set pool only for an embedded or Linux target where owning the descriptors directly matters more than the dependency.
pitfalls: Blocking inside a ChannelHandler stalls every channel owned by that event loop; the loop's thread is its only demultiplexer and cannot be replaced.
NIO objects belong to their event loop: touching a channel or promise from another thread is a data race, so hop back with eventLoop.execute or use the async APIs.
The group is a real thread pool owned by your code; skipping syncShutdownGracefully leaks threads and blocks a clean exit.
Adding or removing handlers on live channels must respect the pipeline's thread confinement rules, not just the handler's own locking.
